queries: SELECT b.tick, b.balance, b.debt, b.treasury, b.income_tax_revenue, b.other_spend, w.capacity, w.demand, w.load_ratio, p.demand_kw, p.supply_kw, p.outage_fraction, m.population, m.net, c.satisfaction FROM budget_monthly b JOIN water_monthly w USING (run_id,tick) JOIN power_monthly p USING (run_id,tick) JOIN migration_monthly m USING (run_id,tick) JOIN (SELECT run_id,tick,avg(satisfaction) satisfaction FROM citizen_monthly GROUP BY run_id,tick) c USING (run_id,tick) ORDER BY b.tick DESC LIMIT 12

SELECT tick, income_tax_rate, property_tax_rate, electricity_tariff, road_maintenance_budget, water_sewer_capex, transit_fare, zoning_release, power_contract_mode FROM lever_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, avg(wear) avg_wear, max(wear) max_wear, avg(congestion) avg_congestion FROM road_monthly GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
turns.rationale: The immediate failures are structural: roads are deteriorating toward complete ruin, water capacity is only modestly above demand and still outside the safe load range, while high electricity and transit prices are suppressing disposable income and satisfaction. The city has ample treasury, so I will fund recovery directly rather than over-rely on taxation, but raise income tax to the documented debt/reserve level to sustain operations. I’ll also switch to hedged power procurement.

SELECT b.tick,b.treasury,b.debt,b.balance,b.road_spend,b.water_sewer_spend,w.capacity,w.demand,w.load_ratio FROM budget_monthly b JOIN water_monthly w USING(run_id,tick) WHERE b.tick BETWEEN 0 AND 63 ORDER BY b.tick DESC LIMIT 30
turns.rationale: The first intervention exposed a sharper water-capacity shock than the initial snapshot implied: capacity fell from 2,464 to 1,094 in three months despite capex, driving a 1.91 load ratio and the satisfaction collapse. Road repair is working (wear fell from 0.97 to 0.42), and hedging reduced outages. I will push water investment to the legal maximum while keeping enough road funding to remain effective; the high tax is temporarily necessary because the treasury was nearly exhausted and debt was incurred during the shock.
